parties:
Ruhul Amin (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Latif Bawani Jute Mills Ltd and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
7. Ms Rezina Mahmud, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the learned Advocate Mr Md Nur Hussain Chowdhury for the petitioner, has placed both the judgments before me and submits that both the Courts below committed a gross error of law in not considering the date of birth of the plaintiff as disclosed in his application for appointment being 2-1-1946 and supported by the passport granted by the Government of Bangladesh on 16-2-1997 mentioning the date of birth of the plaintiff as 2-1-1946 and in not holding that the plaintiff shall be 60 years on 2-1-2006 and not on 30-11-2000 as held by the trial Court and affirmed by the lower appellate Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the Photostat Copy of pages of the register Exhibit Kha is not a reliable document to determine the age of the plaintiff for the purpose of retirement on his completion of 60 years age and the Courts below misconstrued Exhibit Kha. According to the learned Advocate, both the Courts below made a wrong approach to the facts and circumstances of the case and upon misconception of law and facts held that the plaintiff's age of retirement should be 23-11-2000 which is inconsistent with the date of birth of the plaintiff as disclosed for the first time in his application. 

 9. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused both oral and documentary evidence. It is not disputed that the plaintiff joined service in defendant No. I mill on 25-11-1963. It is not also disputed that the retirement age is 60 years. The plaintiff disclosed his date of birth as 24-1946 when he joined his service on 25-11-1963. The contesting defendant did not deny such averment but submits that all the connected papers were destroyed during liberation war in 1971. There is no consistent evidence as regard date of birth of the plaintiff produced by the defendants. The contesting defendant produced few pages of several registers of the Mill Exhibit Kha, Exhibit Cha and Exhibit Chha. The contesting defendant also produced a letter under memo No. LBJM/ LO/2000/dated 3-5-2000 which is a letter issued by the General Manager of Latif Bawani Jute Mills Ltd authorising one Md Zahurul Kabir, ACO (Labour) of the said jute mill to become a witness on behalf of the mill in title suit No. 270 of 1999. This Exhibit Ka has not proved anything. Exhibit Kha is a photostat copy of a page of a register which was relied upon by the Courts below in determining age of the plaintiff. On a perusal of Exhibit Kha it appears that after the name Ruhul Amin 23 was mentioned. That 23 was accepted as the age of the plaintiff. This photostat copy of Exhibit Kha contains the date 25-11-1963 on which date the plaintiff joined the service. This photostat copy Exhibit Kha does not contain signature of any officer of the jute mill. This Exhibit Kha also relates to another worker of the jute mill named Ibrahim Khan (24) who joined on 4-2-71. This photostat copy Exhibit Kha is not a reliable piece of evidence to determine the age of the plaintiff. The Courts below committed error of law in determining the age of the plaintiff on the basis of Exhibit Kha alone. I have already noticed that the date of birth as disclosed by the plaintiff being 2-1-1946 was not disputed by the contesting defendant but the case of the defendant was that all the connected papers were destroyed during war of liberation in 1971. The plaintiff to prove his date of birth being 2-1-1946 has produced his passport Exhibit 3 issued under the signature of the Deputy Assistant Director. Immigration and Passports, Government of Bangladesh, Dhaka on 16-2-1997 and the date of birth as mentioned in the passport is 2-1-1946. This passport being a public document could be accepted as a conclusive evidence to prove the date of birth of the plaintiff in the absence of any other reliable documentary evidence. In the facts of the case, I therefore, accept the date of birth of the plaintiff as 2-1-1946 as clearly mentioned in his passport issued on 16-2-1997 long before the date of the retirement of the plaintiff on 23-11-1999. It could not therefore, be imagined that the plaintiff with motive mentioned the date of birth in his passport to get benefit in the service even after he attains the age of retirement being 60 years. The reason assigned by the learned Additional District Judge for not accepting the passport is not at all acceptable. The lower appellate Court held “এবং বাদী পক্ষের দাখিলী পাসপোর্ট যাতে বাদীর বয়স ২/১/১৯৪৬ উল্লেখ রহিয়াছে। এবং উক্ত পাসপোর্ট বাদীর যে বয়স উল্লেখ করা হইয়াছে তাহা বাদীপক্ষ সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ দ্বারা প্রমাণ করিতে পারে নাই। The lower appellate Court further held যেহেতু বাদী পক্ষের দাখিলকৃত পাসপোর্টটি বাদীর ঘোষনা অনুয়ায়ী উল্লেখ করা হয় সেহেতু বাদীর মূল ঘোষিত বয়স যথাযথভারে প্রদান না হওয়ার উক্ত পাসপোর্টে উল্লিখিত বয়স গ্রহণ যোগ্য নহে।” This finding of the lower appellate Court is totally incorrect and based on misconception of law and facts. Passport, being a public document issued by the Government of Bangladesh, should be accepted as valid document regarding the age mentioned therein for the purpose of determining the age of the passport holder in the absence of any objection raised by the adverse party with regard to date of birth of the passport holder. This passport was admitted as Exhibit 3 without any objection. The plaintiff as PW 1 proved his case regarding his date of birth also in his evidence. PW 2 Shamsuddin Ahmed is the maternal uncle of the plaintiff who proved the date of birth of the plaintiff being 2-1-1946 as declared in affidavit before a notary public. In view of the aforesaid facts I am of the view that the plaintiff has succeeded in proving his date of birth as 2-1-1946 and he attained age of 60 years on 2-1-2006. The plaintiff is therefore entitled to go on retirement on 2-1-2006 and is entitled to all his arrear wages and other benefits. The decisions of the Courts below are therefore not sustainable.
